properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 4 to 10
feet expected in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through late Monday
night. For the High Surf Advisory, from 11 PM this evening to

properties.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Typhoon Warning issued October 17 at 10:39PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
* WHAT...Typhoon conditions, including winds of 64 knots or more
are expected.

* WHERE...Guam and Rota Coastal Waters.

* WHEN...Damaging winds are occurring in eastern waters, and will
begin later tonight in western waters. Onset of destructive winds
after midnight with typhoon force winds early Sunday morning.
Damaging winds will continue into at least Sunday night, especially
if Champi slows down.

* IMPACTS...Destructive to typhoon force winds will produce
dangerous to deadly seas that could damage, capsize or sink
vessels, along with drastically reducing visibilities in heavy
rain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Typhoon Champi (29W) continues to move quickly
toward the Marianas. The exact path of 29W remains subject to
change. However, guidance supports a passage through Guam coastal
waters, a little south of Guam, with damaging winds moving in late
tonight and lasting into at least Sunday night. Champi is expected
to strengthen further as it approaches, then move through the
region as a category 4 super typhoon Sunday morning. Seas are
quickly rising, with significant sea heights reaching as high as
35 feet near the eye wall of Champi. Dangerous sea conditions may
continue into Monday.
properties.instruction:
Prepare for the passage of a
category 4 typhoon Sunday morning. Secure all vessels. Conditions are
expected to be catastrophic for small craft, and extremely dangerous
for any vessels of larger size. As Typhoon Champi approaches, stay
in safe harbor.

* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, strong longshore
currents in the surf zone. For the Coastal Flood Warning, 2 to
4 feet of inundation above ground level expected in low-lying
areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf
Advisory, large breaking waves of 6 to 12 feet expected in the
surf zone.

* WHERE...Ocracoke Island.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, from 8 AM EDT this
morning through this evening. For the Coastal Flood Warning,
from 5 PM this afternoon to 8 AM EDT Tuesday. For the High
Surf Advisory, from midnight tonight to 8 PM EDT Monday.

expected in some areas near shorelines and tidal waterways
resulting in an elevated threat of property damage. Flooding
will extend inland from the waterfront threatening some homes
and businesses. Numerous road closures and flooding of vehicles
will be possible. Vulnerable portions of NC-12 may be inundated,
especially around high tide. There is a possibility of being
stranded on Ocracoke for multiple days. This could be life
threatening if you have an emergency. Dangerous swimming and
surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Strong longshore
currents will create dangerous swimming conditions.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...This has the potential to be a long
duration event bringing more significant ocean overwash
impacts to vulnerable oceanside areas through multiple high
tide cycles into next week. Minor soundside water level rises
will also be possible.

properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued October 17 at 3:27AM CDT until October 17 at 8:00PM CDT by NWS New Orleans LA
properties.description:
...CRITICAL FIRE WEATHER CONDITIONS POSSIBLE TODAY...

.A cold front is introducing some very dry air with RH values
falling into the low to mid 30s along with windy conditions with
some gusts well into the 30 mph range. Winds are expected to
continue in the mid 20 mph range today. The combination of gusty
winds, current drought conditions, ample dry fuel, and very dry
conditions will allow any fire that develops to spread quickly. A
Red Flag Warnings will continue for a large portion of the area
today. This headline will drop by Sunday, but only the wind speeds
will cause this change. The dry, breezy conditions will remain
causing favorable conditions for fire spread.

* AFFECTED AREA...Pointe Coupee, West Feliciana, East Feliciana,
St. Helena, Washington, Iberville, West Baton Rouge, East
Baton Rouge, Assumption, St. James, Wilkinson, Amite, Pike,
Northern Tangipahoa, Walthall, Southeast St. Tammany, Pearl
River, Northern St. Tammany, Southwestern St. Tammany,
Hancock, Central Tangipahoa, Harrison, Lower Tangipahoa,
Jackson, Northern Livingston, Southern Livingston, Western
Ascension and Eastern Ascension.

* WINDS...North 15 to 20 mph with gusts up to 30 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 30 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fire that develops will catch and spread
quickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of
strong winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures can
contribute to extreme fire behavior.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding
expected. For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large breaking
waves up to 35 feet for Guam, 20 to 25 feet for Rota, and 15 to 20
feet for Tinian and Saipan.

* WHERE...Guam, Rota, Tinian and Saipan.

* WHEN...From 5 PM this afternoon to 4 AM ChST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low-lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure will
be inundated. Shoreline erosion will occur. Breaking waves can
sweep people off their feet, and into dangerous seas. Life-
threatening swimming conditions and significant beach erosion can
be expected. Coastal inundation of 5 to 7 feet for Guam, 2 to 4
feet for Rota and 1 to 3 feet for Tinian and Saipan is possible
along with coastal flooding and beach erosion.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Surf is expected to rise rapidly to dangerous
levels tonight. Coastal impacts to the western coasts of Guam and
Rota are highly dependent on the final track of Champi; passage
south of Guam would be reduced impacts whereas passage over Guam
would result in larger coastal inundation.
properties.instruction:
Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay well away from the coast.

properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued October 16 at 6:02PM CDT until October 17 at 8:00PM CDT by NWS Lake Charles LA
properties.description:
...RED FLAG WARNING FOR PORTIONS OF SOUTHEAST TEXAS AND CENTRAL
AND SOUTHWEST LOUISIANA FRIDAY AND SATURDAY...

.Breezy and dry conditions due to a frontal passage will combine
with very dry fuels resulting in a period of high fire danger.
Red flag conditions will develop across portions of central and
southwest Louisiana and southeast Texas Friday afternoon and
evening, before winds decrease and humidity recovers some
overnight. Red flag conditions will then be expected again across
all of central and southwest Louisiana and southeast Texas during
the day Saturday.

032 Evangeline, Fire Weather Zone 033 St. Landry, Fire Weather
Zone 044 Lafayette, Fire Weather Zone 045 Upper St. Martin,

Zone 243 Southern Acadia, Fire Weather Zone 252 Lower
Vermilion, Fire Weather Zone 253 Lower Iberia, Fire Weather
Zone 254 Lower St. Mary, Fire Weather Zone 261 Southern
Jasper, Fire Weather Zone 262 Southern Newton, Fire Weather
Zone 515 Upper Jefferson, Fire Weather Zone 516 Northern
Orange, Fire Weather Zone 615 Lower Jefferson and Fire Weather
Zone 616 Southern Orange.

* TIMING...From 9 AM to 8 PM CDT Saturday.

* WINDS...North 15 to 25 mph with gusts up to 35 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 31 percent.

* TEMPERATURES...Up to 73.

* IMPACTS...Any fire that develops will catch and spread
quickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of
strong winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures can
contribute to extreme fire behavior.
